questions.text: Two harmonic waves moving in the same direction superimpose to form a wave x = a \cos(1.5t) \cos(50.5t) where t is in seconds. Find the period with which they beat (close to nearest integer)
questions.solution:
x = \frac{a}{2}[\cos(52t) + \cos(49t)].
2\pi f_1 = 52, 2\pi f_2 = 49 \implies f_{\text{Beat}} = f_1 - f_2 = \frac{3}{2\pi}\text{ Hz}.
T_{\text{Beat}} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ s} \approx 2.09\text{ s} \approx 2\text{ s}.

questions.text: Two plane polarized light waves combine at a certain point whose electric field components are E_1 = E_0 \sin\omega t and E_2 = E_0 \sin(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{3}). Find the amplitude of the resultant wave.
questions.solution: E = \sqrt{E_0^2 + E_0^2 + 2E_0^2 \cos\frac{\pi}{3}} = \sqrt{3}E_0 \approx 1.73 E_0 \approx 1.7 E_0.

questions.text: A wire of resistance R is bent into a triangular pyramid as shown in figure with each segment having same length. The resistance between points A and B is R/n. The value of n is :
questions.solution:
Each of the 6 segments has resistance r = R/6.
Between terminals A and B, the remaining 4 resistors form a balanced Wheatstone bridge of equivalent resistance r.
In parallel with branch AB (resistance r):
\frac{1}{R_{AB}} = \frac{1}{r} + \frac{1}{2r} + \frac{1}{2r} = \frac{2}{r} \implies R_{AB} = \frac{r}{2} = \frac{R}{12}.
Thus n = 12.

questions.text:
Uniform magnetic fields of different strengths (B_1 and B_2), both normal to the plane of the paper exist as shown in the figure. A charged particle of mass m and charge q, at the interface at an instant, moves into the region 2 with velocity v and returns to the interface. It continues to move into region 1 and finally reaches the interface. What is the displacement of the particle during this movement along the interface ?

(Consider the velocity of the particle to be normal to the magnetic field and B_2 > B_1)
questions.solution:
In region 2, the particle makes a semicircle of diameter 2R_2 = \frac{2mv}{qB_2}.
In region 1, it completes a semicircle of diameter 2R_1 = \frac{2mv}{qB_1}.
The net displacement along the interface is AC = 2R_1 - 2R_2 = \frac{2mv}{qB_1}(1 - \frac{B_1}{B_2}) = \frac{mv}{qB_1}(1 - \frac{B_1}{B_2}) \times 2.

questions.text: If \epsilon_0 denotes the permittivity of free space and \Phi_E is the flux of the electric field through the area bounded by the closed surface, then dimension of (\epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}) are that of :
questions.solution: \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt} = i_d \text{ (displacement current)}, \text{which has the dimensions of electric current } [A].

questions.text:
A rod of length 5\text{ L} is bent right angle keeping one side length as 2\text{ L}.

The position of the centre of mass of the system:
(Consider \text{L} = 10\text{ cm})
questions.solution:
Horizontal segment of length 2L = 20\text{ cm} \implies \text{mass } 2m\text{ at }(10, 0)\text{ cm}.
Vertical segment of length 3L = 30\text{ cm} \implies \text{mass } 3m\text{ at }(0, 15)\text{ cm}.
x_{\text{com}} = \frac{2m(10)+3m(0)}{5m} = 4\text{ cm}, \quad y_{\text{com}} = \frac{2m(0)+3m(15)}{5m} = 9\text{ cm}.
\vec{r}_{\text{com}} = 4\hat{i} + 9\hat{j}.

questions.text: The percentage increase in magnetic field (B) when space within a current carrying solenoid is filled with magnesium (magnetic susceptibility \chi_{\text{mg}} = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}) is :
questions.solution: \%\text{ increase} = \frac{B_{\text{new}}-B_0}{B_0}\times 100\% = (\mu_r - 1)\times 100\% = \chi_m \times 100\% = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \times 100\% = 1.2 \times 10^{-3}\% = \frac{6}{5}\times 10^{-3}\%.

questions.text:
A lens having refractive index 1.6 has focal length of 12\text{ cm}, when it is in air. Find the focal length of the lens when it is placed in water.
(Take refractive index of water as 1.28)
questions.solution:
\frac{1}{f_{\text{air}}} = (1.6 - 1)(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}) \implies \frac{1}{12} = 0.6 K \implies K = \frac{10}{72}.
\frac{1}{f_{\text{water}}} = (\frac{1.6}{1.28}-1) K = (1.25 - 1)\frac{10}{72} = \frac{1}{4}\times\frac{10}{72} = \frac{1}{28.8} \implies f = 28.8\text{ cm} = 288\text{ mm}.
i_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{I_{\text{dc}}^2 + \frac{I_0^2}{2}} = \sqrt{(5\sqrt{2})^2 + \frac{10^2}{2}} = \sqrt{50 + 50} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ Amp}.

questions.text: Two thin convex lenses of focal lengths 30\text{ cm} and 10\text{ cm} are placed coaxially, 10\text{ cm} apart. The power of this combination is :
In the following circuit, the reading of the ammeter will be (Take Zener breakdown voltage = 4\text{ V})
questions.solution:
Open circuit voltage across 400\Omega is V = \frac{400}{100+400}\times 12 = \frac{48}{5} = 9.6\text{ V} > 4\text{ V}.
Zener breakdown occurs, fixing voltage across 400\Omega at 4\text{ V}.
Ammeter reading I = \frac{4\text{ V}}{400\Omega} = 10\text{ mA}.

questions.text: Two projectiles are fired from ground with same initial speeds from same point at angles (45^\circ + \alpha) and (45^\circ - \alpha) with horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flights is
questions.solution: \frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{\sin(45^\circ+\alpha)}{\sin(45^\circ-\alpha)} = \frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos\alpha + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin\alpha}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos\alpha - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin\alpha} = \frac{\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha} = \frac{1+\tan\alpha}{1-\tan\alpha}.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II :

| List-I | List-II |
| :--- | :--- |
| (A) Triatomic rigid gas | (I) \frac{C_p}{C_v} = \frac{5}{3} |
| (B) Diatomic non-rigid gas | (II) \frac{C_p}{C_v} = \frac{7}{5} |
| (C) Monoatomic gas | (III) \frac{C_p}{C_v} = \frac{4}{3} |
| (D) Diatomic rigid gas | (IV) \frac{C_p}{C_v} = \frac{9}{7} |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
\gamma = 1 + \frac{2}{f}.
Triatomic rigid (f=6) \implies \gamma = 4/3 \implies (A)-(III).
Diatomic non-rigid (f=7) \implies \gamma = 9/7 \implies (B)-(IV).
Monoatomic (f=3) \implies \gamma = 5/3 \implies (C)-(I).
Diatomic rigid (f=5) \implies \gamma = 7/5 \implies (D)-(II).

questions.text: A cubic block of mass m is sliding down on an inclined plane at 60^\circ with an acceleration of \frac{g}{2}, the value of coefficient of kinetic friction is
questions.solution: mg\sin 60^\circ - \mu mg\cos 60^\circ = m\frac{g}{2} \implies g\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \mu g\frac{1}{2} = \frac{g}{2} \implies \mu = \sqrt{3}-1.

questions.text: In a hydrogen like ion, the energy difference between the 2^{\text{nd}} excitation energy state and ground is 108.8\text{ eV}. The atomic number of the ion is
questions.solution:
2^{\text{nd}} \text{ excited state corresponds to } n=3.
\Delta E = 13.6 Z^2 (1 - \frac{1}{9}) = 13.6 Z^2 (\frac{8}{9}) = 108.8\text{ eV} \implies Z^2 = \frac{108.8 \times 9}{13.6 \times 8} = 9 \implies Z = 3.

questions.text: For a hydrogen atom, the ratio of the largest wavelength of Lyman series to that of the Balmer series is.
questions.solution:
Lyman largest wavelength (n=2 \to 1): \frac{1}{\lambda_1} = R(1 - \frac{1}{4}) = \frac{3R}{4} \implies \lambda_1 = \frac{4}{3R}.
Balmer largest wavelength (n=3 \to 2): \frac{1}{\lambda_2} = R(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9}) = \frac{5R}{36} \implies \lambda_2 = \frac{36}{5R}.
\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2} = \frac{4/(3R)}{36/(5R)} = \frac{4}{3}\times\frac{5}{36} = \frac{5}{27}.

questions.text: A particle of charge q, mass m and kinetic energy E enters in magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity and undergoes a circular arc of radius (r). Which of the following curves represents the variation of r with E?
questions.solution:
r = \frac{mv}{qB} = \frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{qB} \propto \sqrt{E}.
The curve r \propto \sqrt{E} is parabolic concave downwards (curve (4)).

questions.text: An object of mass 1000\text{ g} experiences a time dependent force \vec{F} = (2t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j})\text{N}. The power generated by the force at time t is :
questions.solution:
m = 1\text{ kg}.
\vec{a} = 2t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j} \implies \vec{v} = t^2\hat{i} + t^3\hat{j}.
P = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{v} = (2t\hat{i}+3t^2\hat{j})\cdot(t^2\hat{i}+t^3\hat{j}) = (2t^3 + 3t^5)\text{ W}.

questions.text: Two wires A and B are made of same material having ratio of lengths \frac{L_A}{L_B} = \frac{1}{3} and their diameters ratio \frac{d_A}{d_B} = 2. If both the wires are stretched using same force, what would be the ratio of their respective elongations?
questions.solution: \Delta L = \frac{FL}{AY} = \frac{4FL}{\pi d^2 Y} \implies \frac{\Delta L_A}{\Delta L_B} = (\frac{L_A}{L_B})(\frac{d_B}{d_A})^2 = (\frac{1}{3})(\frac{1}{2})^2 = \frac{1}{12}.

questions.text: Two charges q_1 and q_2 are separated by a distance of 30\text{ cm}. A third charge q_3 initially at 'C' as shown in the figure, is moved along the circular path of radius 40\text{ cm} from C to D. If the difference in potential energy due to movement of q_3 from C to D is given by \frac{q_3 K}{4\pi\epsilon_0}, the value of K is :
questions.solution:
V_C = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}[\frac{q_1}{0.4} + \frac{q_2}{\sqrt{0.4^2+0.3^2}}] = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}[\frac{q_1}{0.4} + \frac{q_2}{0.5}].
V_D = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}[\frac{q_1}{0.4} + \frac{q_2}{0.1}].
\Delta U = q_3(V_D - V_C) = \frac{q_3}{4\pi\epsilon_0} q_2 (\frac{1}{0.1} - \frac{1}{0.5}) = \frac{q_3(8q_2)}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \implies K = 8q_2.

questions.text:
A, B and C are disc, solid sphere and spherical shell respectively with same radii and masses. These masses are placed as shown in figure.

The moment of inertia of the given system about PQ is \frac{x}{15}I, where I is the moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter. The value of x is _______.

For ac circuit shown in figure, R = 100\text{ k}\Omega and C = 100\text{ pF} and the phase difference between V_{\text{in}} and (V_B - V_A) is 90^\circ. The input signal frequency is 10^x\text{ rad/sec}, where 'x' is _______.
questions.solution:
\theta + \theta = 90^\circ \implies \theta = 45^\circ.
\tan\theta = \frac{X_C}{R} = 1 \implies X_C = R \implies \frac{1}{\omega C} = R \implies \omega = \frac{1}{RC} = \frac{1}{100\times 10^3 \times 100\times 10^{-12}} = 10^5\text{ rad/s} \implies x = 5.

questions.text:
A container contains a liquid with refractive index of 1.2 up to a height of 60\text{ cm} and another liquid having refractive index 1.6 is added to height H above first liquid. If viewed from above, the apparent shift in the position of bottom of container is 40\text{ cm}. The value of H is _______ cm.
(Consider liquids are immiscible)
questions.solution: \text{Shift} = H(1 - \frac{1}{1.6}) + 60(1 - \frac{1}{1.2}) = 40 \implies H(\frac{0.6}{1.6}) + 60(\frac{0.2}{1.2}) = 40 \implies \frac{6}{16}H + 10 = 40 \implies \frac{3}{8}H = 30 \implies H = 80\text{ cm}.

questions.text:
A wire of length 10\text{ cm} and diameter 0.5\text{ mm} is used in a bulb. The temperature of the wire is 1727^\circ\text{C} and power radiated by the wire is 94.2\text{ W}.

Its emissivity is \frac{x}{8} where x = _______
(Given \sigma = 6.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ W m}^{-2}\text{ K}^{-4}, \pi = 3.14 and assume that the emissivity of wire material is same at all wavelength.)
questions.solution:
T = 1727 + 273 = 2000\text{ K}.
A = \pi d L = 3.14 \times 0.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 10 \times 10^{-2} = 1.57 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2.
P = \epsilon\sigma A T^4 \implies 94.2 = \epsilon \times 6.0 \times 10^{-8} \times 1.57 \times 10^{-4} \times (2000)^4 = \epsilon \times 150.72 \implies \epsilon = \frac{94.2}{150.72} = \frac{5}{8} \implies x = 5.

questions.text:
An ideal gas has undergone through the cyclic process as shown in the figure. Work done by the gas in the entire cycle is _______ \times 10^{-1}\text{ J}.
(Take \pi = 3.14)
questions.solution: W = \text{Area of ellipse} = \frac{\pi}{4}(P_2 - P_1)(V_2 - V_1) = \frac{3.14}{4} (500 - 300)\times 10^3 \text{ Pa} \times (350 - 150)\times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^3 = \frac{3.14}{4} \times 200 \times 10^3 \times 200 \times 10^{-6} = 3.14 \times 10 = 31.4\text{ J} = 314 \times 10^{-1}\text{ J}.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Ozonolysis followed by treatment with \text{Zn}, \text{H}_2\text{O} of cis-2-butene gives ethanal.
Statement II : The production obtained by ozonolysis followed by treatment with \text{Zn}, \text{H}_2\text{O} of 3, 6-dimethyloct-4-ene has no chiral carbon atom.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

options.label: B
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II are true

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.label: D
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution:
Statement I is true (cis-2-butene gives 2 moles of ethanal).
Statement II is false (3,6-dimethyloct-4-ene gives 2-methylbutanal, which has a chiral carbon atom \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\overset{*}{\text{C}}\text{H}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHO}).

questions.text: Which of the following amine (s) show (s) positive carbylamines test ?
questions.solution:
Only primary (1^\circ) amines give positive carbylamine test.
A (Aniline) and C (Methylamine) are 1^\circ amines, whereas B and E are 2^\circ amines and D is a 3^\circ amine.

questions.text:
Reaction \text{A}(g) \rightarrow 2\text{B}(g) + \text{C}(g) is a first order reaction. It was started with pure \text{A}

| t/\text{min} | \text{Pressure of system at time } t/\text{mm Hg} |
| :--- | :--- |
| 10 | 160 |
| \infty | 240 |

Which of the following option is incorrect ?

options.label: A
options.text: Initial pressure of A is 80 mm Hg

options.label: B
options.text: The reaction never goes to completion

options.label: C
options.text: Rate constant of the reaction is 1.693 \text{ min}^{-1}

options.label: D
options.text: Partial pressure of A after 10 minute is 40 mm Hg

questions.solution:
P_\infty = 3P_0 = 240\text{ mm Hg} \implies P_0 = 80\text{ mm Hg}.
At t=10\text{ min}, P_t = P_0 + 2x = 160 \implies x = 40\text{ mm Hg} \implies P_A = 80 - 40 = 40\text{ mm Hg}.
k = \frac{1}{10}\ln(\frac{80}{40}) = \frac{\ln 2}{10} = 0.0693\text{ min}^{-1} \neq 1.693\text{ min}^{-1}. Hence option (3) is incorrect.

questions.text:
Total enthalpy change for freezing of 1\text{ mol} of water at 10^\circ\text{C} to ice at -10^\circ\text{C} is _______
(Given : \Delta_{\text{fus}}\text{H} = x\text{ kJ/mol},
C_p[\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)] = y\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1},
C_p[\text{H}_2\text{O}(s)] = z\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1})

An aqueous solution of \text{HCl} with \text{pH } 1.0 is diluted by adding equal volume of water (ignoring dissociation of water). The \text{pH} of \text{HCl} solution would
(Given \log 2 = 0.30)
questions.solution:
[\text{H}^+]_i = 10^{-1}\text{ M}.
Upon doubling volume, [\text{H}^+]_f = \frac{10^{-1}}{2} = 5\times 10^{-2}\text{ M}.
\text{pH} = 1 + \log 2 = 1 + 0.30 = 1.3.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Dimethyl ether is completely soluble in water. However, diethyl ether is soluble in water to a very small extent.
Statement II : Sodium metal can be used to dry diethyl ether and not ethyl alcohol.
In the light of given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.label: A
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II are true

options.label: B
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.label: D
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution:
Statement I is true (lower ethers like dimethyl ether have high solubility via H-bonding, whereas higher hydrocarbon chains decrease solubility).
Statement II is true (sodium reacts with alcohols liberating H_2, but does not react with ethers).

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct, if the threshold frequency of caesium is 5.16 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz} ?
A. When \text{Cs} is placed inside a vacuum chamber with an ammeter connected to it and yellow light is focused on \text{Cs} the ammeter shows the presence of current.
B. When the brightness of the yellow light is dimmed, the value of the current in the ammeter is reduced.
C. When a red light is used instead to the yellow light, the current produced is higher with respect to the yellow light.
D. When a blue light is used, the ammeter shows the formation of current.
E. When a white light is used, the ammeter shows formation of current.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.label: C
options.text: A, C, D and E Only

options.label: D
options.text: A, B, D and E Only

questions.solution:
\lambda_0 = \frac{c}{\nu_0} = \frac{3\times 10^8}{5.16\times 10^{14}} \approx 581.4\text{ nm} \text{ (yellow light range)}.
Red light (\lambda > 600\text{ nm}) has frequency below threshold, so no photoelectric emission occurs.
Dimming light decreases intensity, hence decreasing current.
Blue light and white light contain frequencies above threshold. Thus A, B, D, E are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct IUPAC name of given organic compound (X) ?
questions.solution: Numbering from the carbon attached to -CH_2Br: C1 carries -Br, C2 has methyl group and double bond at C2, giving 1-Bromo-2-methylbut-2-ene.

questions.text:
At the sea level, the dry air mass percentage composition is given as nitrogen gas : 70.0, oxygen gas : 27.0 and argon gas : 3.0. If total pressure is 1.15\text{ atm}, then calculate the ratio of followings respectively :
(i) partial pressure of nitrogen gas to partial pressure of oxygen gas
(ii) partial pressure of oxygen gas to partial pressure of argon gas
(Given : Molar mass of \text{N}, \text{O} and \text{Ar} are 14, 16, and 40\text{ g mol}^{-1} respectively)

Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Mohr's salt is composed of only three types of ions-ferrous, ammonium and sulphate.
Statement II : If the molar conductance at infinite dilution of ferrous, ammonium and sulphate ions are x_1, x_2 and x_3\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}, respectively then the molar conductance for Mohr's salt solution at infinite dilution would be given by x_1 + x_2 + 2x_3
In the light of the given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both statements I and Statement II are false

options.label: B
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.label: D
options.text: Both statements I and Statement II are true

questions.solution:
Mohr's salt is \text{FeSO}_4\cdot(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}.
It dissociates into \text{Fe}^{2+}, 2\text{NH}_4^+, 2\text{SO}_4^{2-}.
By Kohlrausch's law, \Lambda_m^\circ = x_1 + 2x_2 + 2x_3.
Thus Statement I is true and Statement II is false.

questions.text: The number of valence electrons present in the metal among \text{Cr}, \text{Co}, \text{Fe} and \text{Ni} which has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation is
questions.solution:
Among Cr, Fe, Co, Ni in 3d series, Cr has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation due to stable half-filled d-subshell.
Cr has electron configuration [\text{Ar}]3d^5 4s^1, giving 6 valence electrons.

questions.text: When a salt is treated with sodium hydroxide solution it gives gas \text{X}. On passing gas \text{X} through reagent \text{Y} a brown coloured precipitate is formed. \text{X} and \text{Y} respectively, are
questions.solution:
Ammonium salt with NaOH gives \text{NH}_3 (gas X).
\text{NH}_3 with Nessler's reagent (\text{K}_2[\text{HgI}_4] + \text{KOH}) gives brown ppt of iodide of Millon's base.

questions.text: The group 14 elements \text{A} and \text{B} have the first ionisation enthalpy values of 708 and 715\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} respectively. The above values are lowest among their group members. The nature of their ions \text{A}^{2+}, \text{B}^{4+} respectively is
questions.solution:
Group 14 IE values: \text{Sn} (708\text{ kJ/mol}) and \text{Pb} (715\text{ kJ/mol}).
For Sn, +4 is more stable than +2, so \text{Sn}^{2+} is reducing.
For Pb, due to inert pair effect, +2 is more stable than +4, so \text{Pb}^{4+} is oxidising.

questions.text: The first transition series metal 'M' has the highest enthalpy of atomisation in its series. One of its aquated ion (\text{M}^{n+}) exists in green colour. The nature of the oxide formed by the above \text{M}^{n+} ion is :
questions.solution:
In 3d series, Vanadium (V) has the highest enthalpy of atomisation.
\text{V}^{3+} aquated ion is green in colour.
The oxide formed by \text{V}^{3+} is \text{V}_2\text{O}_3, which is basic.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds is least likely to give effervescence of \text{CO}_2 in presence of aq. \text{NaHCO}_3?
questions.solution:
Picric acid (1), p-nitrobenzoic acid (2), and anilinium chloride (3) are all stronger acids than \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3 and liberate \text{CO}_2 with \text{NaHCO}_3.
m-Nitrophenol (4) is a weaker acid than \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3 (pK_a \approx 8.35 vs 6.35) and does not give effervescence with \text{NaHCO}_3.

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II.

| LIST-I (Molecule/ion) | LIST-II (Bond pair : lone pair on the central atom) |
| :--- | :--- |
| (A) \text{ICl}_2^- | (I) 4 : 2 |
| (B) \text{H}_2\text{O} | (II) 4 : 1 |
| (C) \text{SO}_2 | (III) 2 : 3 |
| (D) \text{XeF}_4 | (IV) 2 : 2 |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
\text{ICl}_2^-: 2\text{ bp} + 3\text{ lp} \implies (A)-(III).
\text{H}_2\text{O}: 2\text{ bp} + 2\text{ lp} \implies (B)-(IV).
\text{SO}_2: 4\text{ bonds (2 } \sigma + 2\pi\text{) or 2 } \sigma\text{-bp} + 1\text{ lp} (4:1) \implies (C)-(II).
\text{XeF}_4: 4\text{ bp} + 2\text{ lp} \implies (D)-(I).

questions.text:
A person's wound was exposed to some bacteria and then bacteria growth started to happen at the same place. The wound was later treated with some antibacterial medicine and the rate of bacterial decay (r) was found to be proportional with the square of the existing number of bacteria at any instance. Which of the following set of graphs correctly represents the 'before' and 'after' situation of the application of the medicine?
[Given : \text{N} = \text{No. of bacteria}, \text{t} = \text{time}, \text{bacterial growth follows I}^{\text{st}}\text{ order kinetics.}]
questions.solution:
Before: 1st order growth \implies N = N_0 e^{kt}, so N/N_0 starts at 1 and increases exponentially.
After: r \propto N^2 \implies r = kN^2, which is an upward parabola passing through origin (0, 0).
This matches option (2).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : \text{D-(+)-glucose} + \text{D-(+) fructose} \xrightarrow{-\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{sucrose} \xrightarrow{\text{Hydrolysis}} \text{D-(+)-glucose} + \text{D-(+) fructose}
Statement II : Invert sugar is formed during sucrose hydrolysis.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below -

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

options.label: B
options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II are true.

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.solution:
Statement I is false because fructose obtained from sucrose is \text{D-(-)-fructose} (levorotatory).
Statement II is true because the hydrolysed mixture of glucose and fructose is levorotatory, called invert sugar.

questions.text: An octahedral complex having molecular composition \text{Co}\cdot 5\text{NH}_3\cdot\text{Cl}\cdot\text{SO}_4 has two isomers \text{A} and \text{B}. The solution of \text{A} gives a white precipitate with \text{AgNO}_3 solution and the solution of \text{B} gives white precipitate with \text{BaCl}_2 solution. The type of isomerism exhibited by the complex is,
questions.solution:
Complex A is [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{SO}_4)]\text{Cl} which gives AgCl ppt with \text{AgNO}_3.
Complex B is [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4 which gives \text{BaSO}_4 ppt with \text{BaCl}_2.
These are ionisation isomers.

questions.text:
The reactions which cannot be applied to prepare an alkene by elimination, are

Choose the correct answer from the option given below :
questions.solution:
Reaction B uses aqueous KOH, which causes nucleophilic substitution (SN2) to give alcohol, not elimination.
Reaction D is oxidation of phenol with \text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 to benzoquinone.
Reactions A, C, and E all yield alkenes via elimination.
Hence B and D cannot be applied to prepare an alkene by elimination.

questions.solution:
\text{Mass of carbon} = 220\text{ mg} \times \frac{12}{44} = 60\text{ mg}.
\%\text{ C} = \frac{60\text{ mg}}{500\text{ mg}}\times 100\% = 12\%.

Thyroxine, the hormone has given below structure

questions.text:
1 Faraday electricity was passed through \text{Cu}^{2+} (1.5\text{ M}, 1\text{ L})/\text{Cu} and 0.1 Faraday was passed through \text{Ag}^+ (0.2\text{ M}, 1\text{ L})/\text{Ag} electrolytic cells. After this the two cells were connected as shown below to make an electrochemical cell. The emf of the cell thus formed at 298\text{ K} is _______ \text{mV}.

Given : E_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}}^\circ = 0.34\text{ V}, E_{\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}}^\circ = 0.8\text{ V}, \frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.06\text{ V}
questions.solution:
After passing 1 F through \text{Cu}^{2+}: \text{moles reacted} = 1/2 = 0.5\text{ mol} \implies [\text{Cu}^{2+}] = 1.5 - 0.5 = 1.0\text{ M}.
After passing 0.1 F through \text{Ag}^+: \text{moles reacted} = 0.1\text{ mol} \implies [\text{Ag}^+] = 0.2 - 0.1 = 0.1\text{ M}.
Cell reaction: \text{Cu}(s) + 2\text{Ag}^+(aq) \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{Ag}(s).
E^\circ = 0.80 - 0.34 = 0.46\text{ V}.
E = E^\circ - \frac{0.06}{2}\log\frac{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]}{[\text{Ag}^+]^2} = 0.46 - 0.03\log\frac{1.0}{(0.1)^2} = 0.46 - 0.03(2) = 0.40\text{ V} = 400\text{ mV}.

questions.text: The number of paramagnetic complex among [\text{FeF}_6]^{3-}, [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-}, [\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}, [\text{Co(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}, [\text{MnCl}_6]^{3-} and [\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}, which involved d^2sp^3 hybridization is _______.
questions.solution:
Paramagnetic inner orbital complexes (d^2sp^3): [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3-} (d^5, t_{2g}^5 e_g^0, 1 unpaired e^-, d^2sp^3) and [\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-} (d^4, t_{2g}^4 e_g^0, 2 unpaired e^-, d^2sp^3).
[\text{Co(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-} is d^2sp^3 but diamagnetic (t_{2g}^6).
[\text{FeF}_6]^{3-}, [\text{MnCl}_6]^{3-}, [\text{CoF}_6]^{3-} are outer orbital (sp^3d^2).
Thus exactly 2 complexes.

If the shortest distance between the lines \frac{x-1}{2} = \frac{y-2}{3} = \frac{z-3}{4} and \frac{x}{1} = \frac{y}{\alpha} = \frac{z-5}{1} is \frac{5}{\sqrt{6}}, then the sum of all possible values of \alpha is

Let y = y(x) be the solution curve of the differential equation x(x^2 + e^x)dy + (e^x(x - 2)y - x^3)dx = 0, x > 0, passing through the point (1, 0). Then y(2) is equal to :
questions.solution:
\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{e^x(x-2)}{x(x^2+e^x)}y = \frac{x^2}{x^2+e^x}.
\text{I.F.} = 1 + \frac{e^x}{x^2}.
y(1 + \frac{e^x}{x^2}) = \int \frac{x^2}{x^2+e^x}(\frac{x^2+e^x}{x^2})dx = x + C.
Passing through (1, 0) \implies C = -1.
y(\frac{x^2+e^x}{x^2}) = x - 1 \implies y = \frac{x^2(x-1)}{x^2+e^x}.
For x = 2: y(2) = \frac{4(1)}{4+e^2} = \frac{4}{4+e^2}.

questions.text: From a group of 7 batsmen and 6 bowlers, 10 players are to be chosen for a team, which should include atleast 4 batsmen and atleast 4 bowlers. One batsmen and one bowler who are captain and vice-captain respectively of the team should be included. Then the total number of ways such a selection can be made, is
questions.solution:
Captain (batsman) and vice-captain (bowler) already selected.
We need 8 more players from remaining 6 batsmen and 5 bowlers, such that total batsmen \ge 4 (so \ge 3 more from 6) and total bowlers \ge 4 (so \ge 3 more from 5).
Possible selections of (batsmen, bowlers) from (6, 5):
(3, 5): \binom{6}{3}\binom{5}{5} = 20 \times 1 = 20.
(4, 4): \binom{6}{4}\binom{5}{4} = 15 \times 5 = 75.
(5, 3): \binom{6}{5}\binom{5}{3} = 6 \times 10 = 60.
Total = 20 + 75 + 60 = 155.

questions.text: If for \theta \in [-\frac{\pi}{3}, 0], the points (x, y) = (3\tan(\theta + \frac{\pi}{3}), 2\tan(\theta + \frac{\pi}{6})) lie on xy + \alpha x + \beta y + \gamma = 0, then \alpha^2 + \beta^2 + \gamma^2 is equal to :
questions.solution:
x = 3\frac{\tan\theta + \sqrt{3}}{1 - \sqrt{3}\tan\theta} \implies \tan\theta = \frac{x-3\sqrt{3}}{3+\sqrt{3}x}.
y = 2\frac{\tan\theta + 1/\sqrt{3}}{1 - \tan\theta/\sqrt{3}} \implies \tan\theta = \frac{\sqrt{3}y-2\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}+y}.
Equating expressions gives xy - 2\sqrt{3}x + 3\sqrt{3}y - 6 = 0 \implies \alpha = -2\sqrt{3}, \beta = 3\sqrt{3}, \gamma = -6.
\alpha^2 + \beta^2 + \gamma^2 = 12 + 27 + 36 = 75.

questions.text: Let C_1 be the circle in the third quadrant of radius 3, that touches both coordinate axes. Let C_2 be the circle with centre (1, 3) that touches C_1 externally at the point (\alpha, \beta). If (\beta - \alpha)^2 = \frac{m}{n}, \gcd(m, n) = 1, then m + n is equal to :
questions.solution:
C_1\text{ centre } A(-3, -3), r_1 = 3.
C_2\text{ centre } B(1, 3), r_2 = AB - r_1 = \sqrt{4^2+6^2} - 3 = 2\sqrt{13} - 3.
Point P(\alpha, \beta) divides AB in ratio r_1 : r_2 = 3 : (2\sqrt{13}-3).
\beta - \alpha = y_P - x_P = \frac{3(3)-3(-3)}{2\sqrt{13}} = \frac{6}{2\sqrt{13}} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}.
(\beta - \alpha)^2 = \frac{9}{13} \implies m = 9, n = 13 \implies m + n = 22.

questions.text: The integral \int_0^\pi \frac{(x+3)\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x} dx is equal to :
questions.solution:
I = \int_0^\pi \frac{(x+3)\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x}dx.
\text{Using King's property}, 2I = (\pi+6)\int_0^\pi \frac{\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x}dx = 2(\pi+6)\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x}dx.
\text{Put } \sqrt{3}\cos x = t: I = \frac{\pi+6}{\sqrt{3}}\int_0^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{dt}{1+t^2} = \frac{\pi+6}{\sqrt{3}}(\frac{\pi}{3}) = \frac{\pi}{3\sqrt{3}}(\pi+6).

questions.text:
Among the statements
(S1) : The set \lbrace z \in \mathbb{C} - \lbrace -i \rbrace : |z| = 1 \text{ and } \frac{z-i}{z+i} \text{ is purely real}\rbrace contains exactly two elements, and
(S2) : The set \lbrace z \in \mathbb{C} - \lbrace -1 \rbrace : |z| = 1 \text{ and } \frac{z-1}{z+1} \text{ is purely imaginary}\rbrace contains infinitely many elements.
questions.solution:
For S1: |z|=1, \frac{z-i}{z+i} purely real \implies \frac{z-i}{z+i} = \frac{\bar{z}+i}{\bar{z}-i} \implies (z-i)(\bar{z}-i) = (\bar{z}+i)(z+i) \implies -i(z+\bar{z}) = i(z+\bar{z}) \implies z+\bar{z}=0 \implies \text{Re}(z)=0.
Since |z|=1 and z \neq -i, z = i (only 1 element). So (S1) is false.
For S2: |z|=1 \implies \frac{z-1}{z+1} = \frac{e^{i\theta}-1}{e^{i\theta}+1} = \frac{i\sin(\theta/2)}{\cos(\theta/2)} = i\tan(\theta/2), which is purely imaginary for all \theta \neq \pi. Thus S2 contains infinitely many elements. (S2) is correct.

Let the set of all values of p \in \mathbb{R}, for which both the roots of the equation x^2 - (p + 2)x + (2p + 9) = 0 are negative real numbers, be the interval (\alpha, \beta]. Then \beta - 2\alpha is equal to

2. \text{Sum of roots} = p+2 < 0 \implies p < -2.
3. \text{Product of roots} = 2p+9 > 0 \implies p > -9/2.

\beta - 2\alpha = -4 - 2(-9/2) = -4 + 9 = 5.

questions.text: Let the line L pass through (1, 1, 1) and intersect the lines \frac{x-1}{2} = \frac{y+1}{3} = \frac{z-1}{4} and \frac{x-3}{1} = \frac{y-4}{2} = \frac{z}{1}. Then, which of the following points lies on the line L?
questions.solution:
General point on L_1: A(2\lambda+1, 3\lambda-1, 4\lambda+1).
General point on L_2: B(\mu+3, 2\mu+4, \mu).
Point C(1, 1, 1) lies on L. Direction ratios of CA and CB must be proportional:
\frac{2\lambda}{\mu+2} = \frac{3\lambda-2}{2\mu+3} = \frac{4\lambda}{\mu-1}.
From 1st and 3rd: \frac{2}{\mu+2} = \frac{4}{\mu-1} \implies 2\mu+4 = \mu-1 \implies \mu = -5.
For \mu=-5: \frac{3\lambda-2}{-7} = \frac{2\lambda}{-3} \implies -9\lambda + 6 = -14\lambda \implies 5\lambda = -6 \implies \lambda = -6/5.

questions.text: Let the angle \theta, 0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2} between two unit vectors \hat{a} and \hat{b} be \sin^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt{65}}{9}). If the vector \vec{c} = 3\hat{a} + 6\hat{b} + 9(\hat{a}\times\hat{b}), then the value of 9(\vec{c}\cdot\hat{a}) - 3(\vec{c}\cdot\hat{b}) is
questions.solution:
\sin\theta = \frac{\sqrt{65}}{9} \implies \cos\theta = \sqrt{1 - \frac{65}{81}} = \frac{4}{9}.
\hat{a}\cdot\hat{b} = \cos\theta = \frac{4}{9}.
\vec{c}\cdot\hat{a} = 3|\hat{a}|^2 + 6(\hat{a}\cdot\hat{b}) = 3 + 6(4/9) = \frac{51}{9}.
\vec{c}\cdot\hat{b} = 3(\hat{a}\cdot\hat{b}) + 6|\hat{b}|^2 = 3(4/9) + 6 = \frac{22}{3}.
9(\vec{c}\cdot\hat{a}) - 3(\vec{c}\cdot\hat{b}) = 9(51/9) - 3(22/3) = 51 - 22 = 29.

questions.text: Let ABC be the triangle such that the equations of lines AB and AC be 3y - x = 2 and x + y = 2, respectively, and the points B and C lie on x-axis. If P is the orthocentre of the triangle ABC, then the area of the triangle PBC is equal to
questions.solution:
A is intersection of 3y-x=2 and x+y=2 \implies 4y = 4 \implies y=1, x=1 \implies A(1, 1).
B is intersection of 3y-x=2 with y=0 \implies B(-2, 0).
C is intersection of x+y=2 with y=0 \implies C(2, 0).
Base BC has length 2 - (-2) = 4.
Altitude from A to BC is x = 1.
Altitude from B to AC (slope of AC = -1 \implies slope of altitude = 1): y - 0 = 1(x + 2) \implies y = x + 2.
Intersection gives orthocentre P(1, 3).
Area of \Delta PBC = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3 = 6.

questions.text: The number of points of discontinuity of the function f(x) = [\frac{x^2}{2}] - [\sqrt{x}], x \in [0, 4], where [\cdot] denotes the greatest integer function is _______.
questions.solution:
Points where x^2/2 or \sqrt{x} is integer in [0, 4]: x \in \lbrace 0, 1, \sqrt{2}, 2, \sqrt{6}, \sqrt{8}, \sqrt{10}, \sqrt{12}, \sqrt{14}, 4\rbrace.
At x=0 and x=4, limits match right/left values.
At x=\sqrt{2}, [x^2/2] jumps from 0 to 1 while [\sqrt{x}] stays 1, resulting in jump discontinuity.
Checking all points gives exactly 8 points of discontinuity.

questions.text: The number of relations on the set A = \lbrace 1, 2, 3\rbrace containing at most 6 elements including (1, 2), which are reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, is _______.
questions.solution:
Reflexive implies (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3) must be in R. Since (1, 2) \in R, R contains at least 4 elements.
1. Exactly 4 elements: \lbrace (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (1, 2)\rbrace is transitive and not symmetric (1 way).
2. Exactly 5 elements: adding (1, 3) gives \lbrace (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (1, 2), (1, 3)\rbrace (transitive, not symmetric). Adding (3, 2) gives \lbrace (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (1, 2), (3, 2)\rbrace (transitive, not symmetric) (2 ways).
3. Exactly 6 elements: \lbrace (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (1, 2), (2, 3), (1, 3)\rbrace, \lbrace (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (1, 2), (1, 3), (3, 2)\rbrace (transitive, not symmetric) (2 ways).
Total = 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 relations.

questions.text: Consider the hyperbola \frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1 having one of its focus at P(-3, 0). If the latus rectum through its other focus subtends a right angle at P and a^2 b^2 = \alpha\sqrt{2} - \beta, \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{N}, then \alpha + \beta is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
ae = 3. Other focus is F_2(3, 0).
Latus rectum endpoints: L_1(3, b^2/a), L_2(3, -b^2/a).
Angle L_1 P L_2 = 90^\circ \implies \tan 45^\circ = \frac{b^2/a}{2ae} = 1 \implies \frac{b^2}{a} = 2ae = 6 \implies b^2 = 6a.
Also a^2 e^2 = a^2 + b^2 = 9 \implies a^2 + 6a - 9 = 0 \implies a = -3 + 3\sqrt{2} = 3(\sqrt{2}-1).
a^2 b^2 = a^2 (6a) = 6a^3 = 6[3(\sqrt{2}-1)]^3 = 162(5\sqrt{2} - 7) = 810\sqrt{2} - 1134 \implies \alpha = 810, \beta = 1134 \implies \alpha + \beta = 1944.

questions.text: The number of singular matrices of order 2, whose elements are from the set \lbrace 2, 3, 6, 9\rbrace is _______.
questions.solution:
\det [[a, b], [c, d]] = ad - bc = 0 \implies ad = bc.
Total assignments:
1. All 4 elements identical: 4 ways.
2. 2 distinct elements used twice: e.g. ad = 6 = 2 \times 3 \implies bc = 6 \implies 8 ways, etc.
Summing all valid cases gives 36 singular matrices.

questions.text: For n \ge 2, let S_n denote the set of all subsets of \lbrace 1, 2, \dots, n\rbrace with no two consecutive numbers. For example \lbrace 1, 3, 5\rbrace \in S_6, but \lbrace 1, 2, 4\rbrace \notin S_6. Then n(S_5) is equal to _______.
questions.solution:
For a set of 5 elements:
Subsets with 0 elements: \binom{6}{0} = 1.
Subsets with 1 element: \binom{5}{1} = 5.
Subsets with 2 non-consecutive elements: \binom{5-2+1}{2} = \binom{4}{2} = 6.
Subsets with 3 non-consecutive elements: \binom{5-3+1}{3} = \binom{3}{3} = 1.
Total = 1 + 5 + 6 + 1 = 13.
